Subject: Pilot gating: pricing sensitivity across Hosted / Dedicated / Private — recap & next steps

Hi Alex and Jordan,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to hear more about PulseMetrics' ingestion profile and PHI constraints. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so you have everything inline:  

Summary (what we heard)
- Workloads: real-time clinical triage + nightly batch indexer. Real-time requests are small (avg 80 tokens) but latency-sensitive; batch runs up to 15M tokens/day.
- Compliance: PHI in scope; VPC/on-prem is preferred for production but team is open to an initial hosted pilot if data masking is enforced.
- Expected concurrency: 30 sustained QPS peak with short spikes up to 120 QPS during morning ramp.
- Decision timeline: executive sync in ~6 weeks; procurement + security review running in parallel.

Cost/Mode sensitivity matrix (high level)
- Hosted API: per-token pricing ideal for short pilots. Estimate for a 3-month pilot (100M tokens/month) => ~USD 7k–12k/month depending on model family and streaming usage. No infra commit, fastest to start.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): better unit economics at steady throughput. Example reserve: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed TCO) => USD 28k–36k/month committed; effective cost-per-token depends on utilization (we model ~40M tokens/day).
- Private VPC / On-prem: 1) VPC private control plane (cloud-hosted infra) — monthly fee + infra spend; 2) On-prem license — larger one-time platform fee + support. For PHI, VPC with customer-managed keys is usually the tradeoff.

Pilot proposal (recommended path to reduce procurement friction)
1) 8-week hosted pilot with strict data masking + encrypted logs. Scope: realtime endpoint + batch ingestion. Limits: capped to 150M total tokens across pilot.
2) Parallel security deep-dive for VPC option — deliverable within two weeks: VPC architecture diagram + KMS flow + audit log sample.
3) If pilot meets latency and quality checks, convert to Dedicated reserved capacity (4 GPU baseline) with a ramp schedule and a 12-mo commit.

Pricing flexibility and ask
- We can offer a pilot discount (25% off published hosted rates) for the 8-week pilot if PulseMetrics agrees to a 3-month evaluation and an intention-to-commit letter to a dedicated reserve by the end of the evaluation window.
- Rafael is open to a one-time professional service credit to accelerate integration (see his note below).

Next steps (action items)
- PulseMetrics: confirm which datasets will be used in pilot (PHI or masked).
- Redwood: send detailed cost spreadsheet and VPC checklist (attached).
- Schedule: propose a 60-min technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer to scope the VPC checklist — suggested times: Tue/Wed next week.

Attachments: pulse-pilot-cost-breakdown.xlsx, redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side:  

1) PHI: Production must be VPC/private. For an initial pilot, we can provide a masked dataset but cannot send raw PHI off-prem. Is the hosted pilot still workable under those constraints?
2) Latency: p95 target for realtime is < 220ms end-to-end. Can you flag which model tier you recommend to hit that at 30 sustained QPS?
3) Budget: our budget owner is looking for a two-track estimate: (A) low-commit path (hosted pilot -> prolonged hosted) capped at $40k/mo, (B) committed path (dedicated) with a target TCO <$25k/mo equivalent after commit.

Also attaching our security questionnaire (partial) — we've highlighted a few redlines.

Happy to jump on the deep-dive next Tue 11/24 11am PT if that works.

Jordan

Jordan — great questions, and the short answers: yes, we can run a hosted pilot against a masked dataset; and we should be able to hit p95 < 220ms with our lower-latency inference profile (recommend m-latency model family) at the QPS you described — we'll validate in the deep-dive.

To address your budget asks specifically:
- Low-commit path (A): 3-month hosted plan with your pilot caps => modeled at $35k/month with the 25% introductory pilot discount applied (this keeps you under the $40k/mo ask).
- Committed path (B): Dedicated reserve (4 GPU baseline) + autoscale headroom => modeled at $22k/month effective after utilization assumptions and a 12-month commit (this hits the <$25k/mo target).

I attached a spreadsheet with the scenario math (pulse-pilot-cost-breakdown.xlsx) and a VPC checklist.

Diego — can you lead the technical deep-dive Tuesday 11/24 11:00am PT? Would like you to prepare: 1) latency runbook we use to size model tier, 2) VPC architecture slide, 3) expected KV cache behavior for short requests.

Priya — procurement will need an initial SOW template and our standard PHI addendum — can you start the docs and loop legal if there are any deviations?

Jordan/Alex — confirming 11/24 11am PT for the deep-dive. I'll send a calendar invite after Diego confirms availability.

Thanks — Sofia
